{{Quote|But as always, his strategy is flawed. If your voice cannot travel to the Soldiers, then you, O Queen, must do the traveling. ''[&hellip;]'' Order your Workers to their places. We travel at once to the juggernauts. You promised us victory. You promised me eternal life. You have broken faith on both.|Nuso Esva and the Queen of the Red|translated=1|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
'''Trevik''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Quesoth]] member of the Quesoth [[Midli]] caste of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quethold]]'s [[Red City]], overseeing the Quesoth [[Workers (Quesoth)|Workers]]. The Midli, who was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on Quethold, had a [[Trevik's family|brother]], [[Jirvin]], who oversaw several Workers that handled equipment in the [[Color/Legends|Red]] [[City/Legends|City]]. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], during an alliance between the [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]] and Quethold's ruler, the [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen of the Red]], Trevik became the [[bowlcarrier]] of the [[Queen of the Red|Queen]], carrying a bowl of [[Nectar/Legends|nectar]] next to her litter and entourage.

The following [[Standard day/Legends|days]], Jirvin forced his brother to use [[Empire of the Hand]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] [[Holocamera/Legends|holocam]] to record Esva's artwork inside the Quesoth [[Dwelling of Guests]] building to prove that the Queen was not Esva's pawn. After doing so, the Red City was [[Attack on the Red City|attacked]] by Thrawn's forces, and the Red monarch was slain by the "[[Storm-hair]]"&mdash;Trevik's nickname for Esva's species. The warlord sent the bowlcarrier to tell the attacking [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] that his [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|forces]] would find him and kill him.

==Biography==
{{Quote|You're going to take a message to Thrawn for me, ''[&hellip;]'' Tell Thrawn that he may think he's won, ''[&hellip;]'' But with my death, his own will not be far off. My followers are still out there, and they're more numerous than he can possibly imagine. No matter where he goes, no matter where he tries to hide, they will find him. You'll tell him that. ''[&hellip;]''&raquo;<br />&laquo;I will tell him.|Nuso Esva and Trevik|translated=1|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
[[File:Thrawn_TFUCG.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Grand Admiral Thrawn, who liberated the Quesoth from Esva's forces]]
Trevik of the Midli of the Seventh of the Red was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Quesoth]] who was a member of the Quesoth [[Midli]] caste of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quethold]]'s [[Red City]], overseeing the Quesoth [[Workers (Quesoth)|Workers]]. The Midli had a [[Trevik's family|brother]], [[Jirvin]], who oversaw a group of Workers handling equipment in the [[Color/Legends|Red]] [[City/Legends|City]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> he became the [[bowlcarrier]] of the [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen of the Red]], and was [[Commanding officer/Legends|commanded]] by the governing [[Circling]] caste's [[Borosiv]], who assisted the [[Queen of the Red|Queen]], to straighten up, copy the Workers' stance, and rise the monarch's bowl higher, which Trevik did. The bowlcarrier then accompanied the Queen's litter and entourage to the [[Dwelling of Guests]] building, where the [[Queen/Legends|monarch's]] allies, the [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]] and his [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], the [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|Chosen]], stayed.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

The Queen drank from Trevik's bowl, and spoke with Esva. At the [[Standard day/Legends|darklight]] [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]], the Midli returned to his [[Trevik's home|home]]; however, a [[Unidentified Circling|Circling]] intercepted him, bringing the new bowlcarrier to another Midli's home, where his brother greeted him. A group of Circlings and Jirvin informed Trevik that the Queen of the Red had become Esva's tool, and that to prove the contrary, the bowlcarrier would have to use a [[Holocamera/Legends|holocam]] to record the dwelling's artwork brought there by the warlord so [[Empire of the Hand]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] could determine if Trevik was correct. He accepted, and did what he was told to do the next day, giving the recordings to his brother at the darkling hour after accompanying the Queen's entourage across the city to meet with Esva. That night, the bowlcarrier slept deeply in contrast to the previous one. The next morning, the Red City was [[Attack on the Red City|attacked]] by Thrawn's forces, and Trevik joined the Queen and Esva at the Dwelling of Guests.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

After the Queen's loudspeakers were broken by the Imperial forces, the [[Quesoth Soldier]]s could not receive the monarch's orders in the [[Quesoth Soldier Speak]] [[Language/Legends|language]], and Esva ordered her to go to Thrawn's [[Transport/Legends|transports]] outside the Red City. Trevik objected, and Esva told the "[[Treason/Legends|traitor]]&mdash;" as he had recorded his artwork on Jirvin's orders, which in fact was the warlord's own ploy&mdash;to be quiet. The Queen then called her ally the true traitor, and she was killed by him along with Borosiv and her entourage shortly after. Esva then ordered Trevik to tell Thrawn that he may have won, but his warriors remained, and they would kill him. The alien's forces were defeated shortly after and the Imperial forces helped rebuild the Red City.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I'm a loyal Midli. More than that, I'm the Queen's own bowlcarrier.&raquo;<br />&laquo;You've been bowlcarrier for a single day, ''[&hellip;]'' Don't make it sound as if your entire past and family honor are at risk.&raquo;<br />&laquo;My past may not be at risk, but my family honor surely is, ''[&hellip;]'' Regardless, I cannot betray my Queen in such a way.|Trevik and a Midli|translated=1|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
A male Quesoth, Trevik was a loyal server of the Queen of the Red. The bowlcarrier was hesitant to betray the Queen when his brother told him to record Esva's artwork, but he was persuaded. The member of the Midli was member of a family. He considered Nuso Esva's multifaceted eyes proper.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Skills and abilities==
The bowlcarrier was able to hold a bowl of nectar for the Queen, and spoke [[Quesoth Common Speak]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|You'll note it has the same texture and color pattern as your official bowlcarrier vest. Once secured there, it will be invisible to even the most strong-eyed observer.|Jirvin|translated=1|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
Trevik wore a textured and patterned [[bowlcarrier vest]] and held a bowl of nectar for his Queen.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Behind the scenes==
Trevik appeared in the [[2011]] novella ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'', written by [[Timothy Zahn]] and included in ''[[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition]]''.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />
